<div class="content">
  <h1>Meshery Compatibility Matrix</h1>
  <h3>meshery-traefik-mesh Integration Tests</h3>
  <p>This page shows all the integration test run on meshery-traefik-mesh in the past.</p><style>
    .edge_visible{
      display: table-row !important;
      visibility: visible !important;
    }
    .stable_visible{
      display: table-row !important;
      visibility: visible !important;
    }
    .checkbox{
      display: flex;
      justify-content: flex-end;
      align-items: center;
      text-align: left;
    }
    td.details {
      background-color: #fafafa;
      cursor:text;
    }
    .edge_test_text{
      margin-right: 20px;
    }
    .status-passing {
      background-color: #56B257 !important;
      color: white !important;
    }
    .status-partial {
      background-color: #EBC017 !important;
      color: white !important;
    }
    .status-failing {
      background-color: #B32700 !important;
      color: white !important;
    }
    .status-default {
      background-color: #6c757d !important;
      color: white !important;
    }
    #test-table tbody tr {
      background-color: #3a3f47 !important;
      color: #ccc;
      cursor: pointer;
    }
    #test-table tbody tr:hover {
      background-color: #3a3f47 !important;
      color: #ccc;
    }
  </style>

  <div class="checkbox">
    <div>
      <input onchange="handleEdgeCheckboxChange();" type="checkbox" id="checkbox_edge" value="Edge Tests" checked />
      <label for="checkbox_edge" class="edge_test_text">Edge Channel</label>
    </div>
    <div>
      <input onchange="handleStableCheckboxChange();" type="checkbox" id="checkbox_stable" value="Stable Tests" checked />
      <label for="checkbox_stable">Stable Channel</label>
    </div>
  </div>

  <table id="test-table" style="text-align: center;">
    <thead>
      <tr>
        <th style="text-align: center;">Status</th>
        <th style="text-align: center;">Meshery Component</th>
        <th style="text-align: center;">Meshery Component Version</th>
        <th style="text-align: center;">Meshery Server Version</th>
        <th style="text-align: center;">Infrastructure</th>
        <th style="text-align: center;">Infrastructure Version</th>

  <script>
    function toggle_visibility(id) {
      var e = document.getElementById(id);
      if (e.style.visibility == "visible") {
        e.style.display = "none";
        e.style.visibility = "hidden";
      } else {
        e.style.display = "table-row";
        e.style.visibility = "visible";
      }
    }

    function handleEdgeCheckboxChange() {
      let e = document.getElementsByClassName("edge");
      let stable = document.getElementsByClassName("stable");
      let stable_box = document.getElementById("checkbox_stable");
      for (let i = 0; i < e.length; i++) {
        if (e[i].classList.contains("edge_visible")) {
          e[i].classList.remove("edge_visible");
          if (!stable_box.checked) {
            stable_box.checked = true;
            handleStableCheckboxChange();
          }
        } else {
          e[i].classList.add("edge_visible");
        }
      }
    }

    function handleStableCheckboxChange() {
      let e = document.getElementsByClassName("stable");
      let edge_box = document.getElementById("checkbox_edge");
      for (let i = 0; i < e.length; i++) {
        if (e[i].classList.contains("stable_visible")) {
          e[i].classList.remove("stable_visible");
          if (!edge_box.checked) {
            edge_box.checked = true;
            handleEdgeCheckboxChange();
          }
        } else {
          e[i].classList.add("stable_visible");
        }
      }
    }
  </script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Quick Start with Docker Extension <img src="/installation/docker/images/docker.svg" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>The Docker Extension for Meshery extends Docker Desktop&rsquo;s position as the developer&rsquo;s go-to Kubernetes environment with easy access to the full capabilities of Meshery&rsquo;s collaborative cloud native management features.</p>
<h2 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h2>
<ul>
<li>You need Docker Desktop version of 4.10 or higher for this.</li>
<li>This document applies only when Docker Desktop uses kubeadm with Kubernetes enabled. If you are using kind, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/">Kind</a> section.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="install-the-docker-meshery-extension">
	Install the Docker Meshery Extension
</h2>
<p>Select one of the following three options to install the Docker Meshery Extension:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/docker/docker-extension/#install-the-docker-meshery-extension">Install the Docker Meshery Extension</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/docker/docker-extension/#using-docker-desktop">Using Docker Desktop</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/docker/docker-extension/#using-docker-hub">Using Docker Hub</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/docker/docker-extension/#using-docker-cli">Using Docker CLI</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/docker/docker-extension/#remove-meshery-as-a-docker-extension">Remove Meshery as a Docker Extension</a></li>
</ul>
<h3 id="using-docker-desktop">
	Using Docker Desktop
</h3>
<p>Navigate to the <strong>Extensions</strong> marketplace of Docker Desktop. Search for Meshery and click the Install button to install the extension.</p>
<p><a href="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-install.png"><img class="content-image" src="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-install.png" alt="Docker Meshery Extension Install"  /></a></p>
<p>Click <strong>Open</strong> when installation is done or click <strong>Meshery</strong> on the left under <strong>Extensions</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-open.png"><img class="content-image" src="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-open.png" alt="Docker Meshery Extension Open"  /></a></p>
<p>Click <strong>Login</strong> to open the <em>Meshery Cloud</em> login page. Log in or sign up and you will be redirected back to Docker Desktop.</p>
<p><a href="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-login.png"><img class="content-image" src="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-login.png" alt="Docker Meshery Extension Login"  /></a></p>
<p>Finally, click <strong>Launch Meshery</strong> to load Meshery Dashboard in a browser window. It runs at http://localhost:9081/ by default.</p>
<p><a href="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-launch.png"><img class="content-image" src="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-launch.png" alt="Docker Meshery Extension Launch"  /></a></p>
<p>You can also open http://localhost:9081/ directly on a browser on the local machine after installing the Docker extension and complete the <em>Meshery Cloud</em> login process to achieve the same result.</p>
<h3 id="using-docker-hub">
	Using Docker Hub
</h3>
<p>Another way to install the Meshery Docker Extension is from the Docker Hub. Navigate to the <a href="https://hub.docker.com/extensions/meshery/docker-extension-meshery">Meshery Docker Extension</a> page and click Open in Docker Desktop to get started. Once installed, the rest of the process is same as above.</p>
<p><a href="/installation/docker/images/docker-hub-meshery-extension.png"><img class="content-image" src="/installation/docker/images/docker-hub-meshery-extension.png" alt="Docker Hub Extension"  /></a></p>
<h3 id="using-docker-cli">
	Using Docker CLI
</h3>
<p>Finally, you can also install the Meshery Docker Extension using the Docker CLI. Follow the commands in the clipboard below.</p>
<!--
{% capture code_content %}docker extension install meshery/docker-extension-meshery{% endcapture %} -->
<!-- {% include code.html code=code_content %} -->
<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="padding: 0; font-size: 0px;">
  <div class="codeblock" style="display: block;">
    <!-- Updated style for clipboardjs -->
    <div class="clipboardjs" style="padding: 0; height: 0.5rem; overflow: hidden;">
      <span style="font-size: 0;">docker extension install meshery/docker-extension-meshery</span> 
    </div>
    <div class="window-buttons"></div>
    <div id="termynal2" style="width: 100%; height: 200px; max-width: 100%;" data-termynal="">
      <span data-ty="input">docker extension install meshery/docker-extension-meshery</span>
      <span data-ty="progress"></span>
      <span data-ty="">Successfully installed Meshery</span>
      <span data-ty="input">mesheryctl system dashboard</span>
    </div>
  </div>
</pre>
<p>It runs as a set of one or more containers inside your Docker Desktop virtual machine.</p>
<p>Finally, you can now fully utilize Meshery to manage and monitor your cloud-native infrastructure.</p>
<h2 id="remove-meshery-as-a-docker-extension">
	Remove Meshery as a Docker Extension
</h2>
<p>You can remove the Docker Extension from the Docker Desktop interface or from the CLI.</p>
<h3 id="removing-from-docker-desktop">
	Removing from Docker Desktop
</h3>
<p>Navigate to <strong>Manage</strong> under Extensions, click the ellipsis button (three vertical dots) and select <strong>Uninstall</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-remove.png"><img class="content-image" src="/installation/docker/images/docker-desktop-meshery-extension-remove.png" alt="Remove Meshery Docker Desktop Extension"  /></a></p>
<h3 id="removing-using-docker-cli">
	Removing using Docker CLI
</h3>
<p>To remove the extension from the command line, use the <code>docker extension rm</code> command.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">$ docker extension rm meshery/docker-extension-meshery</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="additional-cleanup">
	Additional Cleanup
</h3>
<p>There could be residual images and networks to remove after removing/uninstalling the extension. Follow the steps below to do so.</p>
<p><strong>Remove Meshery Images (if necessary)</strong></p>
<p>Meshery pulls Docker images for deploying the extension and there could be additional Meshery images based on how it was configured. You can remove these images using the <code>docker rmi</code> command. Start by listing all the images and then running the command for each image you want to remove. For example:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">docker rmi meshery/meshery:stable-latest</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Remove Meshery Docker Networks (if necessary)</strong></p>
<p>Meshery creates custom Docker networks, and they could still be left after the extension uninstall. These can be removed using the <code>docker network rm</code> command. For example:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">docker network rm meshery_default</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';

            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

<h1>Quick Start with Docker <img src="/installation/docker/images/docker.svg" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>

<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>

1. Install the Meshery command line client, 
<a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">
    mesheryctl
</a>.
</div>
<h2 id="deploying-meshery-on-docker">
	Deploying Meshery on Docker
</h2>
<p>Follow these installation steps to use Docker and Docker Compose to run Meshery. Users often choose this installation approach in order to run Meshery on their local machine. If you need to install <em>Docker</em>, see <a href="https://docs.docker.com/get-started/">Getting Started with Docker</a>, and if you need to install <em>Docker Compose</em>, see <a href="https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/">Installing Docker Compose</a>.</p>
<p>Start Meshery by executing the following command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p docker</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="advanced-configuration">
	Advanced Configuration
</h2>
<h3 id="customizing-kubernetes-configuration-location">
	Customizing Kubernetes Configuration Location
</h3>
<p>By default, Meshery looks for Kubernetes configuration in the <code>$HOME/.kube</code> directory. You can customize this location by setting the <code>KUBECONFIG_FOLDER</code> environment variable in your Docker deployment.</p>
<p>To use a custom kubeconfig location with Docker Compose, modify your <code>docker-compose.yaml</code>:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">services:
  meshery:
    environment:
      - &#34;KUBECONFIG_FOLDER=/custom/path/to/.kube&#34;
    volumes:
      - /custom/path/to/.kube:/custom/path/to/.kube:ro</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>This is useful when:</p>
<ul>
<li>Providing a Meshery deployment with a predefined Kubernetes context</li>
<li>Running Meshery in containerized environments with custom kubeconfig paths</li>
<li>Managing multiple Kubernetes configurations</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h2>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

      <description>&lt;h1&gt;Quick Start with Docker Extension &lt;img src=&#34;/v0.9/installation/docker/images/docker.svg&#34; style=&#34;width:35px;height:35px;&#34; /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The Docker Extension for Meshery extends Docker Desktop&amp;rsquo;s position as the developer&amp;rsquo;s go-to Kubernetes environment with easy access to the full capabilities of Meshery&amp;rsquo;s collaborative cloud native management features.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;You need Docker Desktop version of 4.10 or higher for this.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;This document applies only when Docker Desktop uses kubeadm with Kubernetes enabled. If you are using kind, please refer to the &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/&#34;&gt;Kind&lt;/a&gt; section.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;install-the-docker-meshery-extension&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install the Docker Meshery Extension&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Select one of the following three options to install the Docker Meshery Extension:&lt;/p&gt;</description>

            <h1>Installation</h1>
          
          
<h2 id="supported-platforms">
	Supported Platforms
</h2>
<p>Meshery deploys as a set of Docker containers to either a Docker host or a Kubernetes cluster. A given deployment of Meshery can be described as either an <em>in-cluster</em> or an <em>out-of-cluster</em> deployment. Meshery runs as a standalone management plane on a Docker host (<em>out-of-cluster</em>) or within a Kubernetes cluster (<em>in-cluster</em>). See the complete list of supported platforms below.</p>



<ul class="section-title">

  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/compatibility-matrix/">Compatibility Matrix</a>

        
          - An installation compatibility matrix and project test status dashboard.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/docker/">Docker</a>

        
          - Install Meshery on Docker
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/">Install Meshery CLI on Linux or macOS</a>

        
          - Install Meshery CLI on Linux or macOS
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/windows/">Install Meshery CLI on Windows</a>

        
          - Install Meshery CLI on Windows
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">Kubernetes</a>

        
          - Install Meshery on Kubernetes. Deploy Meshery in Kubernetes in-cluster or outside of Kubernetes out-of-cluster.
        
      </li>
    
  

  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/accessing-meshery-ui/">Accessing Meshery UI</a>

        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/codespaces/">Codespaces</a>

        
          - Build and contribute to Meshery using GitHub Codespaces
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl/">Install mesheryctl</a>

        
          - Install Meshery CLI
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/playground/">Meshery Playground</a>

        
          - Details about Meshery Playground
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/quick-start/">Quick Start Guide</a>

        
          - Getting Meshery up and running locally on a Docker-enabled system or in Kubernetes is easy. Meshery deploys as a set of Docker containers, which can be deployed to either a Docker host or a Kubernetes cluster.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/upgrades/">Upgrading Meshery and all of its components</a>

        
          - How to upgrade Meshery and all of its components
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/installation/multiple-adapters/">Using Multiple Adapters</a>

        
          - Meshery is capable of running zero or more adapters. Meshery offers many features without the need for adapters. Adapters are optional components that enhance and extend Meshery&#39;s core functionality.
        
      </li>
    
  

</ul>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

    <item>
      <title>Accessing Meshery UI</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/accessing-meshery-ui/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/accessing-meshery-ui/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2&gt;Accessing Meshery UI&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery&#39;s web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is &lt;a href=&#34;http://localhost:9081&#34;&gt;http://localhost:9081&lt;/a&gt;).&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34; style=&#34;font-size: 1.75rem !important;&#34;&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA;&lt;code class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;mesheryctl system dashboard&lt;/code&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Codespaces</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/codespaces/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/codespaces/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Use Minikube in GitHub Codespaces to setup your development environment for Meshery.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong style=&#34;font-size: 20px;&#34;&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &#xA;  &lt;ol&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install the Meshery command line client, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;  &lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;available-deployment-methods&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Available Deployment Methods&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;In-cluster Installation&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#preflight-checks&#34;&gt;Preflight Checks&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#preflight-cluster-connectivity&#34;&gt;Preflight: Cluster Connectivity&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#installation-using-mesheryctl&#34;&gt;Installation: Using &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#installation-using-helm&#34;&gt;Installation: Using Helm&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#installation-manual-steps&#34;&gt;Installation: Manual Steps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/codespaces/#post-installation-steps&#34;&gt;Post-Installation Steps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h1 id=&#34;in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;In-cluster Installation&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your Minikube cluster.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;preflight-checks&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Preflight Checks&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Read through the following considerations prior to deploying Meshery on Minikube.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Install mesheryctl</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery&amp;rsquo;s command line client is &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; and is the recommended tool for configuring and deploying one or more Meshery deployments. To install &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; on your system, you may choose from any of the following supported methods.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; can be installed via &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/bash/&#34;&gt;bash&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/brew/&#34;&gt;Homebrew&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/windows/scoop/&#34;&gt;Scoop&lt;/a&gt; or &lt;a href=&#34;https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest&#34;&gt;directly downloaded&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;NOTE&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Mesheryctl is configured for Kubernetes by default. To specify a different supported platform, use the &lt;code&gt;-p&lt;/code&gt; flag.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h1 id=&#34;install-meshery-cli-with-brew&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install Meshery CLI with Brew&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;You need to have &lt;code&gt;Brew&lt;/code&gt; installed on your &lt;strong&gt;Linux&lt;/strong&gt; or &lt;strong&gt;macOS&lt;/strong&gt; system to perform these actions.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Meshery Playground</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/playground/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/playground/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;Try out Meshery Playground at &lt;a href=&#34;https://playground.meshery.io/&#34;&gt;https://playground.meshery.io/&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery Playground is a web-based, collaborative environment that lets you explore Meshery as a cloud native manager and all of the infrastructure it manages, including multiple Kubernetes clusters, CNCF projects and applications, services, and operators that run on Kubernetes. Meshery Playground provides a sandboxed environment to experiment with different infrastructure configurations and deployment options. Its multiplayer plugins allow you to collaborate in real time with your teammates on infrastructure design and operation.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Quick Start Guide</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/quick-start/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/quick-start/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;a name=&#34;getting-started&#34;&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Getting Meshery up and running locally on a Docker-enabled system or in Kubernetes is easy. Meshery deploys as a set of Docker containers, which can be deployed to either a Docker host or Kubernetes cluster.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-warning&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Quick Start Assumptions&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This quick start guide enables you to download, install, and run Meshery in a single command. See all &lt;a href=&#39;/v0.9/installation&#39;&gt;supported platforms&lt;/a&gt; for more specific (and less presumptuous) instructions.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;1-download-install-and-run-meshery&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;1. Download, install, and run Meshery&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;If you are on a macOS or Linux system, you can download, install, and run both &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; and Meshery Server by executing the following command.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Upgrading Meshery and all of its components</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/upgrades/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/upgrades/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1 id=&#34;upgrade-guide&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Upgrade Guide&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;upgrading-meshery-server-adapters-and-ui&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Upgrading Meshery Server, Adapters, and UI&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Various components of Meshery will need to be upgraded as new releases become available. Meshery is comprised of a number of components including a server, adapters, UI, and CLI. As an application, Meshery is a composition of different functional components.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p style=&#34;text-align:center&#34;&gt;&#xA;&lt;a href=&#34;./images/upgrading-meshery.svg&#34;&gt;&#xA;    &lt;img src=&#34;./images/upgrading-meshery.svg&#34; style=&#34;margin: 1rem;&#34; /&gt;&#xA;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br /&gt;&lt;i&gt;&lt;small&gt;Figure: Meshery components&lt;/small&gt;&lt;/i&gt;&#xA;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Some of the components must be upgraded simultaneously, while others may be upgraded independently. The following table depicts components, their versions, and deployment units (deployment groups).&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Using Multiple Adapters</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/multiple-adapters/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/multiple-adapters/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;advanced-configuration&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Advanced Configuration&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery is capable of running zero or more adapters. Meshery offers many features without the need for adapters. Adapters are optional components that enhance and extend Meshery&amp;rsquo;s core functionality.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;modifying-the-default-adapter-deployment-configuration&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Modifying the default adapter deployment configuration&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The number of adapters, type of adapters, where they are deployed, how they are named and what port they are exposed on are all configurable deployment options. To modify the default configuration, find &lt;code&gt;~/.meshery/meshery.yaml&lt;/code&gt; on your system. &lt;code&gt;~/.meshery/meshery.yaml&lt;/code&gt; is a Docker Compose file.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>

          <h1>Quick Start with AKS <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/aks.svg" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>Manage your AKS clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in AKS <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#in-cluster-installation">in-cluster</a> or outside of AKS <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#out-of-cluster-installation">out-of-cluster</a>. <strong><em>Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your AKS clusters</em></strong></p>
<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>
<ol>
<li>Install the Meshery command line client, <a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">mesheryctl</a>.</li>
<li>Install <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/">kubectl</a> on your local machine.</li>
<li>Install <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli">Azure CLI</a>, configured for your environment.</li>
<li>Access to an active AKS cluster in one of your resource groups.</li>
</ol>
</div>
<p>Also see: <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">Install Meshery on Kubernetes</a></p>
<h2 id="available-deployment-methods">
	Available Deployment Methods
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#in-cluster-installation">In-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#preflight-checks">Preflight Checks</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#preflight-cluster-connectivity">Preflight: Cluster Connectivity</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#installation-using-mesheryctl">Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#installation-using-helm">Installation: Using Helm</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#post-installation-steps">Post-Installation Steps</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h1 id="in-cluster-installation">
	In-cluster Installation
</h1>
<p>Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your AKS cluster.</p>
<h3 id="preflight-checks">
	Preflight Checks
</h3>
<p>Read through the following considerations prior to deploying Meshery on AKS.</p>
<h3 id="preflight-cluster-connectivity">
	Preflight: Cluster Connectivity
</h3>
<ol>
<li>Verify you connection to an Azure Kubernetes Services Cluster using Azure CLI.</li>
<li>Login to Azure account using <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/authenticate-azure-cli">az login</a>.</li>
<li>After a successful login, identify the subscription associated with your AKS cluster:</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">az account set --subscription [SUBSCRIPTION_ID]</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ol>
<li>After setting the subscription, set the cluster context.</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">az aks get-credentials --resource-group [RESOURCE_GROUP] --name [AKS_SERVICE_NAME]</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="installation-using-mesheryctl">
	Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code>
</h3>
<p>Use Meshery&rsquo;s CLI to streamline your connection to your AKS cluster. Configure Meshery to connect to your AKS cluster by executing:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system config aks</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Once configured, execute the following command to start Meshery.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>If you encounter any authentication issues, you can use <code>mesheryctl system login</code>. For more information, click <a href="/v0.9/guides/mesheryctl/authenticate-with-meshery-via-cli/">here</a> to learn more.</p>
<h3 id="installation-using-helm">
	Installation: Using Helm
</h3>
<p>For detailed instructions on installing Meshery using Helm V3, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/">Helm Installation</a> guide.</p>
<h2 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h2>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment, using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

          <h1>Quick Start with EKS <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/eks.png" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>Manage your EKS clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in EKS <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#in-cluster-installation">in-cluster</a> or outside of EKS <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#out-of-cluster-installation">out-of-cluster</a>. <strong><em>Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your EKS clusters</em></strong></p>
<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>
  <ol>
    <li>Install the Meshery command line client, <a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">mesheryctl</a>.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/">kubectl</a> on your local machine.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/getting-started.html">AWS CLI</a>, configured for your environment.</li>
    <li>Access to an active EKS cluster in an AWS account.</li>
  </ol>
</div>
<p>Also see: <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">Install Meshery on Kubernetes</a></p>
<h3 id="available-deployment-methods">
	Available Deployment Methods
</h3>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#in-cluster-installation">In-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#installation-using-mesheryctl">Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#installation-using-helm">Installation: Using Helm</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#post-installation-steps">Post-Installation Steps</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#out-of-cluster-installation">Out-of-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#install-meshery-on-docker">Install Meshery on Docker</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h1 id="in-cluster-installation">
	In-cluster Installation
</h1>
<p>Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your EKS cluster.</p>
<p><strong>Prerequisites: Cluster Connectivity</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Verify your connection to an Elastic Kubernetes Service cluster using the AWS CLI.</li>
<li>Log in to your AWS account using <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-authentication-user.html">aws configure</a>. If you are using a different method of authentication in AWS, please refer to AWS documentation.</li>
<li>After successful login, set the cluster context.</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">aws eks update-kubeconfig --name [YOUR_CLUSTER_NAME] --region [YOUR_REGION]</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ol>
<li><em>Optional:</em> If you are using <code>eksctl</code>, follow the <a href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/getting-started-eksctl.html">AWS documentation steps</a>.</li>
<li>Verify your kubeconfig&rsquo;s current context.</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl config current-context</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="installation-using-mesheryctl">
	Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code>
</h2>
<p>Execute <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/start'>mesheryctl system start</a> command to start Meshery.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="installation-using-helm">
	Installation: Using Helm
</h2>
<p>For detailed instructions on installing Meshery using Helm V3, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/">Helm Installation</a> guide.</p>
<h2 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h2>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

<h1 id="out-of-cluster-installation">
	Out-of-cluster Installation
</h1>
<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Out-of-cluster EKS deployments not currently supported</div>
<p>Out-of-cluster support for EKS is still beta and on the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/ROADMAP.md">roadmap</a>.</p>
</div>
<p>Install Meshery on Docker (out-of-cluster) and connect it to your EKS cluster.</p>
<h2 id="install-meshery-on-docker">
	Install Meshery on Docker
</h2>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p docker</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Configure Meshery to connect to your cluster by executing:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system config eks</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Once you have verified that all the services are up and running, Meshery UI will be accessible on your local machine on port 9081. Open your browser and access Meshery at <a href="http://localhost:9081"><code>http://localhost:9081</code></a>.</p>

    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {

                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

          <h1>Quick Start with GKE <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/gke.png" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>Manage your GKE clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in GKE <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#in-cluster-installation">in-cluster</a> or outside of GKE <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#out-of-cluster-installation">out-of-cluster</a>. <strong><em>Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your GKE clusters</em></strong></p>
<div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisites</strong> </p> 
  <ol>
    <li>Install the Meshery command line client, <a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">mesheryctl</a>.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/">kubectl</a> on your local machine.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install">gcloud CLI</a>, configured for your environment.</li>
    <li>Access to an active GKE cluster in your Google Cloud project.</li>
  </ol>
</div>
<p>Also see: <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">Install Meshery on Kubernetes</a></p>
<h2 id="available-deployment-methods">
	Available Deployment Methods
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#in-cluster-installation">In-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#preflight-checks">Preflight Checks</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#preflight-cluster-connectivity">Preflight: Cluster Connectivity</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#preflight-plan-your-access-to-meshery-ui">Preflight: Plan your access to Meshery UI</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#installation-using-mesheryctl">Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#installation-using-helm">Installation: Using Helm</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#post-installation-steps">Post-Installation Steps</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h1 id="in-cluster-installation">
	In-cluster Installation
</h1>
<p>Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your GKE cluster.</p>
<h2 id="preflight-checks">
	Preflight Checks
</h2>
<p>Read through the following considerations prior to deploying Meshery on GKE.</p>
<h3 id="preflight-cluster-connectivity">
	Preflight: Cluster Connectivity
</h3>
<ol>
<li>Verify your connection to a Google Kubernetes Engine Cluster using the gcloud CLI.</li>
<li>Log in to your GCP account using <a href="https://cloud.google.com/sdk/gcloud/reference/auth/login">gcloud auth login</a>.</li>
<li>After a successful login, set the Project Id:</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">gcloud config set project [PROJECT_ID]</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ol>
<li>After setting the Project Id, set the cluster context.</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">gcloud container clusters get-credentials [CLUSTER_NAME] --zone [CLUSTER_ZONE]</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ol>
<li>Verify your kubeconfig&rsquo;s current context.</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl config current-context</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="preflight-plan-your-access-to-meshery-ui">
	Preflight: Plan your access to Meshery UI
</h3>
<ol>
<li>If you are using port-forwarding, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/reference/mesheryctl/system/dashboard/">port-forwarding</a> guide for detailed instructions.</li>
<li>If you are using a LoadBalancer, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#exposing-meshery-serviceloadbalancer">LoadBalancer</a> guide for detailed instructions.</li>
<li>Customize your Meshery Provider Callback URL. Meshery Server supports customizing authentication flow callback URL, which can be configured in the following way:</li>
</ol>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Meshery should now be running in your GKE cluster, and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.</p>
<h2 id="installation-using-mesheryctl">
	Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code>
</h2>
<p>Use Meshery&rsquo;s CLI to streamline your connection to your GKE cluster. Configure Meshery to connect to your GKE cluster by executing:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system config gke</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Once configured, execute the following command to start Meshery.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>If you encounter any authentication issues, you can use <code>mesheryctl system login</code>. For more information, click <a href="/v0.9/guides/mesheryctl/authenticate-with-meshery-via-cli/">here</a> to learn more.</p>
<h2 id="installation-using-helm">
	Installation: Using Helm
</h2>
<p>For detailed instructions on installing Meshery using Helm V3, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/">Helm Installation</a> guide.</p>
<h2 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h2>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1 id="install-meshery-on-kubernetes-using-helm">
	Install Meshery on Kubernetes Using Helm
</h1>
<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>
<ol>
<li><a href="https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/" class="meshery-light">Helm</a> should be installed on your local machine.</li>
<li>You should have access to the cluster/platform where you want to deploy Meshery.</li>
<li>Ensure that the kubeconfig file has the correct current context/cluster configuration.</li>
</ol>
</div>
<h2 id="install-meshery-on-your-kubernetes-cluster-using-helm">
	Install Meshery on Your Kubernetes Cluster Using Helm
</h2>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm repo add meshery https://meshery.io/charts/
helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --create-namespace</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Optionally, Meshery Server supports customizing the callback URL for your remote provider, like so:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --set env.MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host --create-namespace</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="customizing-mesherys-installation-with-valuesyaml">
	Customizing Meshery&rsquo;s Installation with values.yaml
</h3>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s Helm chart supports a number of configuration options. Please refer to the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/install/kubernetes/helm/meshery#readme">Meshery Helm chart</a> and <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/tree/master/install/kubernetes/helm/meshery-operator#readme">Meshery Operator Helm Chart</a> for more information.</p>
<h4 id="configuring-kubernetes-configuration-location">
	Configuring Kubernetes Configuration Location
</h4>
<p>By default, Meshery looks for Kubernetes configuration in the <code>/home/appuser/.kube</code> directory within the container. You can customize this location by setting the <code>KUBECONFIG_FOLDER</code> environment variable:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --set env.KUBECONFIG_FOLDER=/custom/path/to/.kube --create-namespace</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>This is useful when providing a Meshery deployment with a predefined Kubernetes context or when using custom volume mounts for kubeconfig files.</p>
<h2 id="upgrading-meshery-with-helm">
	Upgrading Meshery with Helm
</h2>
<p>To upgrade an existing Meshery deployment:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm repo update
helm upgrade meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>For optimal upgrade performance with health check support, use the upgrade-specific values:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm upgrade meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/meshery/meshery/master/install/kubernetes/helm/meshery/values-upgrade.yaml --wait --timeout 10m</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>The upgrade configuration includes:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Startup probes</strong> to protect pods during initialization</li>
<li><strong>Optimized probe timing</strong> for capability reloading</li>
<li><strong>Higher failure thresholds</strong> to tolerate temporary unavailability during upgrades</li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/install/kubernetes/helm/meshery/HEALTHCHECKS.md">Health Check Configuration Guide</a> for detailed information.</p>
<h2 id="health-checks-and-monitoring">
	Health Checks and Monitoring
</h2>
<p>Meshery implements Kubernetes-compliant health check endpoints that follow best practices from the Kubernetes API server:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Liveness probe</strong> (<code>/healthz/live</code>) - Checks if Meshery is running and responsive</li>
<li><strong>Readiness probe</strong> (<code>/healthz/ready</code>) - Checks if Meshery is ready to accept traffic</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="monitoring-deployment-status">
	Monitoring Deployment Status
</h3>
<p>Monitor the status of your Meshery deployment:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl get pods --namespace meshery -w</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="checking-health-status">
	Checking Health Status
</h3>
<p>Verify health status with detailed information using verbose mode:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl exec --namespace meshery deployment/meshery -- curl -s &#39;http://localhost:8080/healthz/ready?verbose=1&#39;</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Example output:</strong></p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>[+]capabilities ok
[i]extension extension package found
healthz check passed
</code></pre><p><strong>Legend:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><code>[+]</code> - Health check passed</li>
<li><code>[-]</code> - Health check failed (causes pod to be marked unhealthy)</li>
<li><code>[i]</code> - Informational status (does not affect health)</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="health-check-configuration">
	Health Check Configuration
</h3>
<p>The Helm chart includes pre-configured health checks with sensible defaults:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Liveness probe</strong>: Initial delay of 80 seconds to allow for server startup and provider initialization</li>
<li><strong>Readiness probe</strong>: Initial delay of 10 seconds with frequent checks for faster readiness detection</li>
<li><strong>Startup probe</strong>: Optional (disabled by default) for handling slow-starting containers</li>
</ul>
<p>To customize probe settings, modify your <code>values.yaml</code>:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">probe:
  livenessProbe:
    enabled: true
    initialDelaySeconds: 80
    periodSeconds: 12
    failureThreshold: 4
    timeoutSeconds: 5

  readinessProbe:
    enabled: true
    initialDelaySeconds: 10
    periodSeconds: 4
    failureThreshold: 4
    timeoutSeconds: 3</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>For comprehensive guidance on configuring health checks for different scenarios (installation, upgrades, troubleshooting), see the <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/blob/master/install/kubernetes/helm/meshery/HEALTHCHECKS.md">Health Check Configuration Guide</a>.</p>
<h2 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h2>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

    $(document).ready(function () {

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');

                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)

            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {

          let parentCollapse = activeSection.closest(".collapse");
          if (parentCollapse) {

          }
        });
      });
    })();
