<h1>Quick Start with Kubernetes <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/kubernetes.svg" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>Manage your Kubernetes clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in Kubernetes <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#in-cluster-installation">in-cluster</a> or outside of Kubernetes <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#out-of-cluster-installation">out-of-cluster</a>. <strong><em>Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your Kubernetes clusters</em></strong></p>
<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>
  <ol>
    <li>Install the Meshery command line client, <a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">mesheryctl</a>.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/">kubectl</a> on your local machine.</li>
    <li>Access to an active Kubernetes cluster.</li>
  </ol>
</div>
<h2 id="available-deployment-methods">
	Available Deployment Methods
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#in-cluster-installation">In-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#preflight-checks">Preflight Checks</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#preflight-cluster-connectivity">Preflight: Cluster Connectivity</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#installation-using-mesheryctl">Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#installation-using-helm">Installation: Using Helm</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#post-installation-steps">Post-Installation Steps</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#out-of-cluster-installation">Out-of-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#set-up-ingress-on-minikube-with-the-nginx-ingress-controller">Set up Ingress on Minikube with the NGINX Ingress Controller</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/#installing-cert-manager-with-kubectl">Installing cert-manager with kubectl</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h1 id="in-cluster-installation">
	In-cluster Installation
</h1>
<p>Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your Kubernetes cluster.</p>
<h2 id="preflight-checks">
	Preflight Checks
</h2>
<p>Read through the following considerations prior to deploying Meshery on Kubernetes.</p>
<h3 id="preflight-cluster-connectivity">
	Preflight: Cluster Connectivity
</h3>
<p>Verify your kubeconfig&rsquo;s current context is set to the Kubernetes cluster you want to deploy Meshery to.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl config current-context</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="installation-using-mesheryctl">
	Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code>
</h2>
<p>Once configured, execute the following command to start Meshery.</p>
<p>Before executing the below command, go to ~/.meshery/config.yaml and ensure that the current platform is set to Kubernetes.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="installation-using-helm">
	Installation: Using Helm
</h2>
<p>For detailed instructions on installing Meshery using Helm V3, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/">Helm Installation</a> guide.</p>
<h2 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h2>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

<h1 id="out-of-cluster-installation">
	Out-of-cluster Installation
</h1>
<p>Install Meshery on Docker (out-of-cluster) and connect it to your Kubernetes cluster.</p>
<!-- ## Installation: Upload Config File in Meshery Web UI

- Run the below command to generate the _"config_minikube.yaml"_ file for your cluster:

 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">kubectl config view --minify --flatten > config_minikube.yaml</div></div>
 </pre>

- Upload the generated config file by navigating to _Settings > Environment > Out of Cluster Deployment_ in the Web UI and using the _"Upload kubeconfig"_ option. -->
<h2 id="set-up-ingress-on-minikube-with-the-nginx-ingress-controller">
	Set up Ingress on Minikube with the NGINX Ingress Controller
</h2>
<ul>
<li>Run the below command to enable the NGINX Ingress controller for your cluster:</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">minikube addons enable ingress</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<ul>
<li>To check if NGINX Ingress controller is running</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl get pods -n ingress-nginx</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h2 id="installing-cert-manager-with-kubectl">
	Installing cert-manager with kubectl
</h2>
<ul>
<li>Run the below command to install cert-manager for your cluster:</li>
</ul>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.15.3/cert-manager.yaml</code>
	</div>
</pre>

      <title>AKS</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1&gt;Quick Start with AKS &lt;img src=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/aks.svg&#34; style=&#34;width:35px;height:35px;&#34; /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Manage your AKS clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in AKS &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;in-cluster&lt;/a&gt; or outside of AKS &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#out-of-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;out-of-cluster&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;strong&gt;&lt;em&gt;Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your AKS clusters&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;h4&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Install the Meshery command line client, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/&#34;&gt;kubectl&lt;/a&gt; on your local machine.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cli/azure/install-azure-cli&#34;&gt;Azure CLI&lt;/a&gt;, configured for your environment.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Access to an active AKS cluster in one of your resource groups.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Also see: &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/&#34;&gt;Install Meshery on Kubernetes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;available-deployment-methods&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Available Deployment Methods&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;In-cluster Installation&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#preflight-checks&#34;&gt;Preflight Checks&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#preflight-cluster-connectivity&#34;&gt;Preflight: Cluster Connectivity&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#installation-using-mesheryctl&#34;&gt;Installation: Using &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#installation-using-helm&#34;&gt;Installation: Using Helm&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/aks/#post-installation-steps&#34;&gt;Post-Installation Steps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h1 id=&#34;in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;In-cluster Installation&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your AKS cluster.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>EKS</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1&gt;Quick Start with EKS &lt;img src=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/eks.png&#34; style=&#34;width:35px;height:35px;&#34; /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Manage your EKS clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in EKS &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;in-cluster&lt;/a&gt; or outside of EKS &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#out-of-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;out-of-cluster&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;strong&gt;&lt;em&gt;Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your EKS clusters&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;h4&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;  &lt;ol&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install the Meshery command line client, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/&#34;&gt;kubectl&lt;/a&gt; on your local machine.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/getting-started.html&#34;&gt;AWS CLI&lt;/a&gt;, configured for your environment.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Access to an active EKS cluster in an AWS account.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;  &lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Also see: &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/&#34;&gt;Install Meshery on Kubernetes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;available-deployment-methods&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Available Deployment Methods&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;In-cluster Installation&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#installation-using-mesheryctl&#34;&gt;Installation: Using &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#installation-using-helm&#34;&gt;Installation: Using Helm&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#post-installation-steps&#34;&gt;Post-Installation Steps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#out-of-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;Out-of-cluster Installation&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/eks/#install-meshery-on-docker&#34;&gt;Install Meshery on Docker&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h1 id=&#34;in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;In-cluster Installation&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your EKS cluster.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>GKE</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1&gt;Quick Start with GKE &lt;img src=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/gke.png&#34; style=&#34;width:35px;height:35px;&#34; /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Manage your GKE clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in GKE &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;in-cluster&lt;/a&gt; or outside of GKE &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#out-of-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;out-of-cluster&lt;/a&gt;. &lt;strong&gt;&lt;em&gt;Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your GKE clusters&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong style=&#34;font-size: 20px;&#34;&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &#xA;  &lt;ol&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install the Meshery command line client, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/&#34;&gt;kubectl&lt;/a&gt; on your local machine.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install&#34;&gt;gcloud CLI&lt;/a&gt;, configured for your environment.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;    &lt;li&gt;Access to an active GKE cluster in your Google Cloud project.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;  &lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Also see: &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/&#34;&gt;Install Meshery on Kubernetes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;available-deployment-methods&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Available Deployment Methods&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;In-cluster Installation&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#preflight-checks&#34;&gt;Preflight Checks&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#preflight-cluster-connectivity&#34;&gt;Preflight: Cluster Connectivity&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#preflight-plan-your-access-to-meshery-ui&#34;&gt;Preflight: Plan your access to Meshery UI&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#installation-using-mesheryctl&#34;&gt;Installation: Using &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#installation-using-helm&#34;&gt;Installation: Using Helm&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/gke/#post-installation-steps&#34;&gt;Post-Installation Steps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h1 id=&#34;in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;In-cluster Installation&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your GKE cluster.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Helm</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1 id=&#34;install-meshery-on-kubernetes-using-helm&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install Meshery on Kubernetes Using Helm&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;h4&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;Helm&lt;/a&gt; should be installed on your local machine.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;You should have access to the cluster/platform where you want to deploy Meshery.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Ensure that the kubeconfig file has the correct current context/cluster configuration.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;install-meshery-on-your-kubernetes-cluster-using-helm&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install Meshery on Your Kubernetes Cluster Using Helm&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&#x9;&lt;code class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;helm repo add meshery https://meshery.io/charts/&#xA;helm install meshery meshery/meshery --namespace meshery --create-namespace&lt;/code&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Optionally, Meshery Server supports customizing the callback URL for your remote provider, like so:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>KinD</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1&gt;Quick Start with KinD &lt;img src=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/kind.png&#34; style=&#34;width:35px;height:35px;&#34; /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Manage your KinD clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in your &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;KinD cluster&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;h4&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Install the Meshery command line client, &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/&#34;&gt;kubectl&lt;/a&gt; on your local machine.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Install &lt;a href=&#34;https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation&#34;&gt;KinD&lt;/a&gt; on your local machine.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Also see: &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/&#34;&gt;Install Meshery on Kubernetes&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;available-deployment-methods&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Available Deployment Methods&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#available-deployment-methods&#34;&gt;Available Deployment Methods&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;In-cluster Installation&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#preflight-checks&#34;&gt;Preflight Checks&lt;/a&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#preflight-cluster-connectivity&#34;&gt;Preflight: Cluster Connectivity&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#installation-using-mesheryctl&#34;&gt;Installation: Using &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#alternative-installation-using-helm&#34;&gt;Alternative Installation: Using Helm&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#post-installation-steps&#34;&gt;Post-Installation Steps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;in-cluster-installation&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;In-cluster Installation&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your KinD cluster.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>KubeSphere</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kubesphere/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kubesphere/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1&gt;Quick Start with KubeSphere &lt;img src=&#34;/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/kubesphere.png&#34; style=&#34;width:35px;height:35px;&#34; /&gt;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;prereqs&#34;&gt;&lt;h4&gt;Prerequisites&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA;&#xA;1. Install the Meshery command line client, &#xA;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/mesheryctl&#34; class=&#34;meshery-light&#34;&gt;&#xA;    mesheryctl&#xA;&lt;/a&gt;.&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;https://meshery.io/&#34;&gt;Meshery&lt;/a&gt; is the open source, cloud native management plane that enables the adoption, operation, and management of Kubernetes, all kinds of cloud native infrastructure, and their workloads.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This tutorial walks you through an example of deploying Meshery from the App Store of KubeSphere.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Please make sure you enable the OpenPitrix system.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;You need to create a workspace, a project, and a user account (&lt;code&gt;project-regular&lt;/code&gt;) for this tutorial. The account needs to be a platform regular user and to be invited as the project operator with the &lt;code&gt;operator&lt;/code&gt; role. In this tutorial, you log in as &lt;code&gt;project-regular&lt;/code&gt; and work in the project &lt;code&gt;demo-project&lt;/code&gt; in the workspace &lt;code&gt;demo-workspace&lt;/code&gt;. For more information, see Create Workspaces, Projects, Users and Roles.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;hands-on-lab&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Hands-on Lab&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Perform the following steps in order:&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Minikube</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/</guid>
    </item>

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Quick Start with KinD <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/kind.png" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>Manage your KinD clusters with Meshery. Deploy Meshery in your <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#in-cluster-installation">KinD cluster</a>.</p>
<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>
<ol>
<li>Install the Meshery command line client, <a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">mesheryctl</a>.</li>
<li>Install <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/">kubectl</a> on your local machine.</li>
<li>Install <a href="https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/#installation">KinD</a> on your local machine.</li>
</ol>
</div>
<p>Also see: <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">Install Meshery on Kubernetes</a></p>
<h2 id="available-deployment-methods">
	Available Deployment Methods
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#available-deployment-methods">Available Deployment Methods</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#in-cluster-installation">In-cluster Installation</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#preflight-checks">Preflight Checks</a>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#preflight-cluster-connectivity">Preflight: Cluster Connectivity</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#installation-using-mesheryctl">Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#alternative-installation-using-helm">Alternative Installation: Using Helm</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/kind/#post-installation-steps">Post-Installation Steps</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="in-cluster-installation">
	In-cluster Installation
</h2>
<p>Follow the steps below to install Meshery in your KinD cluster.</p>
<h3 id="preflight-checks">
	Preflight Checks
</h3>
<p>Read through the following considerations prior to deploying Meshery on KinD.</p>
<h4 id="preflight-cluster-connectivity">
	Preflight: Cluster Connectivity
</h4>
<p>Start KinD if it is not already started using the following command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kind create cluster</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Check the status of your KinD cluster:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kind get clusters</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Verify your kubeconfig&rsquo;s current context.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl config current-context</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="installation-using-mesheryctl">
	Installation: Using <code>mesheryctl</code>
</h3>
<details>
<summary>Verify your Meshery context</summary>
<p>
Verify that your current Meshery context is set for an in-cluster deployment (<code>platform: kubernetes</code>) by executing:
</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system context view</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>
If the context is not set to <code>platform: kubernetes</code>, you can create a new context with Kubernetes as the platform using the following command.
</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system context create context-name --platform kubernetes --url http://localhost:9081 --set --yes</code>
	</div>
</pre>

</details>
<p>With your KIND cluster configured as your <code>current-context</code>, start Meshery.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p kubernetes</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="alternative-installation-using-helm">
	Alternative Installation: Using Helm
</h3>
<p>See <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/">Helm Installation</a> guide.</p>
<h3 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h3>
<p>Meshery deploys with LoadBalancer service type by default. If you are using KinD, you may need to expose the Meshery service. A universal option is to use <code>mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>. A KIND-specific option is to use the <a href="https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/loadbalancer/">Cloud Provider KIND</a>. Cloud Provider KIND runs as a standalone binary in your host and connects to your KIND cluster and provisions new LoadBalancer containers for your Services.</p>
<p>Note: The <code>--port-forward</code> flag is intended for use exclusively when Meshery is deployed in a Kubernetes cluster (<code>platform: kubernetes</code>).</p>
<p>Optionally, you can verify the health of your Meshery deployment using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to use Meshery! Open your browser and navigate to the Meshery UI.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

        <div class="td-content">
          
          <h1>Quick Start with KubeSphere <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/kubesphere.png" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>

<div class="prereqs"><h4>Prerequisites</h4>

1. Install the Meshery command line client, 
<a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">
    mesheryctl
</a>.
</div>
<p><a href="https://meshery.io/">Meshery</a> is the open source, cloud native management plane that enables the adoption, operation, and management of Kubernetes, all kinds of cloud native infrastructure, and their workloads.</p>
<p>This tutorial walks you through an example of deploying Meshery from the App Store of KubeSphere.</p>
<h2 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h2>
<ul>
<li>Please make sure you enable the OpenPitrix system.</li>
<li>You need to create a workspace, a project, and a user account (<code>project-regular</code>) for this tutorial. The account needs to be a platform regular user and to be invited as the project operator with the <code>operator</code> role. In this tutorial, you log in as <code>project-regular</code> and work in the project <code>demo-project</code> in the workspace <code>demo-workspace</code>. For more information, see Create Workspaces, Projects, Users and Roles.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="hands-on-lab">
	Hands-on Lab
</h2>
<p>Perform the following steps in order:</p>
<h3 id="1-deploy-meshery-from-the-app-store">
	1. <b>Deploy Meshery from the App Store</b>
</h3>
<ol>
<li>
<p>On the <strong>Overview</strong> page of the project <code>demo-project</code>, click <strong>App Store</strong> in the upper-left corner.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Search for <strong>Meshery</strong> in the App Store, and click on the search result to open the app.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/meshery-app.png" alt="meshery-app"  /></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In the <strong>App Information</strong> page, click <strong>Install</strong> on the upper right corner.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/Meshery-install.png" alt="meshery-install"  /></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In the App Settings page, set the application <strong>Name</strong>, <strong>Location</strong> (as your namespace), and <strong>App Version</strong>, then click <strong>Next</strong> on the upper right corner.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/Meshery-info.png" alt="meshery-info"  /></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the <strong>values.yaml</strong> file as needed, or click <strong>Install</strong> to use the default configuration.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/Meshery-yaml.png" alt="meshery-yaml"  /></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Wait for the deployment to be finished. Upon completion, <strong>Meshery</strong> will be shown as <strong>Running</strong> in KubeSphere.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/Meshery-app-running.png" alt="meshery-app-running"  /></p>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="2-access-the-meshery-dashboard">
	2. <b>Access the Meshery Dashboard</b>
</h3>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Go to <strong>Services</strong> and click the service name of Meshery.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In the <strong>Resource Status</strong> page, copy the <strong>NodePort</strong> of Meshery.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/Meshery-service.png" alt="meshery-service"  /></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Access the Meshery Dashboard by entering <strong>${NodeIP}:${NODEPORT}</strong> in your browser.</p>
<p><img class="content-image" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/meshery-dashboard.png" alt="meshery-dashboard"  /></p>
</li>
</ol>

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {

            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {

        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {

            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Minikube</h1>
          
          <h1>Quick Start with Minikube <img src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/minikube.png" style="width:35px;height:35px;" /></h1>
<p>Meshery can manage your minikube clusters and is particularly useful for multi-cluster management and deployments.</p>
<p>For Meshery to manage your Minikube cluster, it has to be discovered and added as a Kubernetes connection in the Meshery server.</p>
<p><strong>There are two ways to create this connection:</strong></p>
<ol>
<li>Deploying Meshery in minikube <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#in-cluster-installation">(in-cluster)</a>.</li>
<li>Deploying Meshery using Docker and connect it to minikube <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#out-of-cluster-installation">(out-of-cluster)</a>.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong><em>Note: It is advisable to install Meshery in your Minikube clusters</em></strong></p>
<div class="prereqs"><p><strong style="font-size: 20px;">Prerequisites</strong> </p> 
  <ol>
    <li>Install the Meshery command-line client, <a href="/installation/mesheryctl" class="meshery-light">mesheryctl</a>.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/">kubectl</a> on your local machine.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io/docs/start/?arch=%2Fmacos%2Fx86-64%2Fstable%2Fbinary+download"> Minikube</a> on your local machine.</li>
    <li>Install <a href="https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/">Helm</a>.</li>
  </ol>
</div>
<p>Also see: <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">Install Meshery on Kubernetes</a></p>
<h2 id="available-deployment-methods">
	Available Deployment Methods
</h2>
<ul>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#preflight-checks">Preflight Checks</a></p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#1-preflight-cluster-connectivity">Preflight: Cluster Connectivity</a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#2-preflight-meshery-authentication">Preflight: Meshery Authentication</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#in-cluster-installation">In-cluster Installation</a></p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#installation-install-meshery-on-kubernetes-using-mesheryctl">Installation: Install Meshery on Kubernetes Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#installation-using-helm">Installation: Using Helm</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#out-of-cluster-installation">Out-of-cluster Installation</a></p>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#installation-install-meshery-on-docker">Installation: Install Meshery on Docker Using <code>mesheryctl</code></a></li>
<li><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#minikube-docker-driver-users">Minikube Docker Driver Users</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#uploading-configuration-file-in-the-meshery-web-ui">Uploading Configuration File in the Meshery Web UI</a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#post-installation-steps">Post-Installation Steps</a></p>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="preflight-checks">
	Preflight Checks
</h2>
<p>Before deploying Meshery on minikube, complete the following initial setup tasks to prepare your environment.</p>
<h3 id="1-preflight-cluster-connectivity">
	1. Preflight: Cluster Connectivity
</h3>
<p>Start minikube using the following command if it is not already running:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">minikube start</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Check the status of your minikube cluster by running:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">minikube status</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Verify that the current context is set to minikube by running:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl config current-context</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="2-preflight-meshery-authentication">
	2. Preflight: Meshery Authentication
</h3>
<p>Ensure you are logged in and <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/mesheryctl/authenticate-with-meshery-via-cli">authenticated with Meshery</a> by running the following command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system login</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h1 id="in-cluster-installation">
	In-cluster Installation
</h1>
<h2 id="installation-install-meshery-on-kubernetes-using-mesheryctl">
	Installation: Install Meshery on Kubernetes Using <code>mesheryctl</code>
</h2>
<p>To install Meshery inside your minikube cluster, run the command:</p>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p kubernetes</code>
	</div>
</pre>

This command deploys the Meshery Helm chart in the Meshery namespace.</p>
<p>To verify your deployment, run:</p>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">helm list -A -n meshery</code>
	</div>
</pre>

After deployment, access the Meshery UI using port forwarding, with the command:</p>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
	</div>
</pre>

For detailed instructions on port forwarding, refer to the <a href="/v0.9/reference/mesheryctl/system/dashboard/">port-forwarding</a> guide.</p>
<p>By default, Meshery auto-detects your Minikube cluster and establishes a connection. However, if this doesn’t happen, you can connect by running the following command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system config minikube</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>The <code>mesheryctl system config minikube</code> command properly configures and uploads your kubeconfig file to the Meshery UI.</p>
<p><a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/minikube-upload.png"><img alt="Minikube KubeConfig Upload" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/images/minikube-upload.png" /></a></p>
<h2 id="installation-using-helm">
	Installation: Using Helm
</h2>
<p>You can deploy Meshery directly using the Helm CLI.
For detailed instructions on installing Meshery using Helm V3, please refer to the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/helm/">Helm Installation</a> guide.</p>
<h1 id="out-of-cluster-installation">
	Out-of-cluster Installation
</h1>
<p>To install Meshery on Docker(out-of-cluster) and connect it to your Minikube cluster, follow these steps:</p>
<h2 id="installation-install-meshery-on-docker">
	Installation: Install Meshery on Docker
</h2>
<p>Run the following command to start Meshery in a Docker environment:</p>
<p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p docker</code>
	</div>
</pre>

This will start Meshery in Docker containers. To verify that Meshery is running, use</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">docker ps</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p>Meshery UI will be accessible on your local machine on port 9081. Open your browser and access Meshery at http://localhost:9081.</p>
<p>Configure Meshery to connect with your minikube cluster by running the command:</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system config minikube</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<h3 id="minikube-docker-driver-users">
	Minikube Docker Driver Users
</h3>
<p>For users running minikube with the Docker driver, specific steps are needed to ensure that Meshery can connect properly to your minikube cluster.</p>
<p>If you set up your minikube cluster using the <a href="https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io/docs/drivers/docker/">Docker driver</a>, both minikube and Meshery will be running in Docker containers. So, you need to ensure that the Meshery and minikube containers can communicate with each other by placing them in the same Docker network.</p>
<p>To configure this, run the following commands:</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">docker network connect bridge meshery-meshery-1</div></div>
</pre>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">docker network connect minikube meshery-meshery-1</div></div>
</pre>
<p>Next, update the Kubernetes API server address in your kubeconfig file before running the <code>mesheryctl system config minikube</code> command. The steps to do this are outlined below.</p>
<h4 id="next-step-update-the-kubernetes-api-server-address-for-meshery-access">
	Next Step: Update the Kubernetes API Server Address for Meshery Access
</h4>
<p>To allow the Meshery container to access your Minikube cluster (since both are running in containers), you need to update the Kubernetes API server address in your <code>kubeconfig file</code> to the <code>external minikube IP address</code>. This is necessary because Docker typically forwards ports to a localhost address, which isn’t accessible between containers.</p>
<p>To retrieve the Minikube IP, run the command <code>minikube ip</code>. To check which port minikube is using, run <code>docker ps</code> to view the container&rsquo;s port, which is typically <code>8443</code>.</p>
<p>Open the kubeconfig file and update the server address.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">nano ~/.kube/config.yaml

## Change the server address

server: https://{minikubeIP}:{port}</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><code>Ctrl + X</code> then enter <code>Y</code> to save and close the file.</p>
<p>Next, run the following command to configure Meshery to access your cluster.</p>


<pre class="codeblock-pre">
	<div class="codeblock">
		<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system config minikube</code>
	</div>
</pre>

<p><strong>Note</strong>: An alternative to running the mesheryctl system config minikube command for Meshery to discover your cluster is manually uploading your config file to the UI.</p>
<h1 id="uploading-configuration-file-in-the-meshery-web-ui">
	Uploading Configuration File in the Meshery Web UI
</h1>
<p><strong>Note</strong>: Meshery can only connect to your cluster if it is running locally (Kubernetes or Docker). Direct connections are not possible when using the hosted <a href="https://playground.meshery.io/">Meshery Playground</a>.</p>
<p><strong>To manually upload your kubeconfig file after running Meshery locally</strong>:</p>
<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on <strong>Connections</strong>.</li>
<li>Click on <strong>Add Cluster</strong> and search for your kubeconfig file.</li>
<li>Click <strong>Import</strong>.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Note</strong>:  If you encounter a connections refused error while uploading your kubeconfig, try changing your cluster server URL to the external API address of minikube. To do this follow the steps listed in the <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/minikube/#docker-driver-update-the-kubernetes-api-server-address-for-meshery-access">Minikube Docker Driver Users Section</a>.</p>
<h4 id="troubleshooting-meshery-installation">
	Troubleshooting Meshery Installation
</h4>
<p>If you experience any issues during installation, refer to the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/guides/troubleshooting/installation#setting-up-meshery-using-kind-or-minikube">Troubleshooting Meshery Installations</a> guide for help.</p>
<h1 id="post-installation-steps">
	Post-Installation Steps
</h1>
<p>Verify the health of your Meshery deployment, using <a href='/reference/mesheryctl/system/check'>mesheryctl system check</a>.</p>

<h2>Accessing Meshery UI</h2>


<p>After successfully deploying Meshery, you can access Meshery's web-based user interface. Your default browser will automatically open and navigate to Meshery UI (default location is <a href="http://localhost:9081">http://localhost:9081</a>).</p>

<p>You can use the following command to open Meshery UI in your default browser:</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>If you have installed Meshery on Kubernetes or a remote host, you can access Meshery UI by exposing it as a Kubernetes service or by port forwarding to Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system dashboard --port-forward</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>Depending on how you have networking configured in Kubernetes, you can use kubectl to port forward to the Meshery UI.</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">kubectl port-forward svc/meshery 9081:9081 --namespace meshery</code>
</div>
</pre>

<h4>Verify Kubernetes Connection</h4>

After installing Meshery, regardless of the installation type, it is important to verify that your kubeconfig file has been uploaded correctly via the UI. 

<ol>
<li>In the Meshery UI, navigate to <strong>Lifecycle</strong> from the menu on the left.</li>
<li>Click on Connections.</li>
<li>Ensure that your cluster appears in the list of connections and is marked as <code>Connected</code>.</li>
<li>Click on the cluster name to perform a ping test and confirm that Meshery can communicate with your cluster.</li>
</ol>

<details>
<summary>Customizing Your Meshery Provider Callback URL</summary>

<p>
  Meshery Server supports customizing your <a href="/extensibility/providers">Meshery Provider</a> authentication flow callback URL. This is helpful when deploying Meshery behind multiple layers of networking infrastructure.
</p>

<p>
  For production deployments, it is recommended to access the Meshery UI by setting up a reverse proxy or using a LoadBalancer. By specifying a custom redirect endpoint, you can ensure that authentication flows complete successfully, even when multiple routing layers are involved.
</p>

<p>
  <b>Note</b>: For production deployments, it is important to select the <code>Remote Provider</code> in order to control which identity providers are authorized. Learn more about this in the <a href="/extensibility/providers">Extensibility: Providers</a> guide.
</p>

<p>
  Define a custom callback URL by setting up the <code>MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL</code> environment variable before installing Meshery.
</p>

<p>
  To customize the authentication flow callback URL, use the following command:
</p>

<pre class="codeblock-pre" style="font-size: 1.75rem !important;">
<div class="codeblock">
<code class="clipboardjs">MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start</code>
</div>
</pre>

<p>
  Meshery should now be running in your Kubernetes cluster and the Meshery UI should be accessible at the <code>EXTERNAL IP</code> of the <code>meshery</code> service.
</p>

</details>

    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

          <h1 id="install-meshery-cli-with-bash">
	Install Meshery CLI with Bash
</h1>
<p>To install or upgrade <code>mesheryctl</code> using <code>bash</code>, execute anyone of the following commands.</p>
<h4 id="option-1-only-install-mesheryctl-binary">
	Option 1: Only install <code>mesheryctl</code> binary
</h4>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | DEPLOY_MESHERY=false bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
#### Option 2: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Docker
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=docker bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
#### Option 3: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Kubernetes
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
#### Option 4: Install `mesheryctl` binary and Meshery adapter(s)
<p>Install <code>mesheryctl</code> binary and include one or more <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/adapters/">adapters</a> to be deployed</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | ADAPTERS=consul PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
### Start Meshery
You are ready to deploy Meshery `mesheryctl`. To do so, execute the following command.
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</div></div>
 </pre>
<p>If you are running Meshery on Docker, execute the following command.</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p docker</div></div>
 </pre>

        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

          <h1 id="install-meshery-cli-with-homebrew">
	Install Meshery CLI with Homebrew
</h1>
<h3 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h3>
<p>You need to have <code>Brew</code> installed on your <strong>Linux</strong> or <strong>macOS</strong> system to perform these actions.</p>
<h3 id="install-mesheryctl-using-brew">
	Install <code>mesheryctl</code> using Brew
</h3>
<p>To install <code>mesheryctl</code> using homebrew, execute the following commands.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew install mesheryctl
 </div></div>
</pre>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>
<p>If you are running Meshery on Docker, execute the following command.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ mesheryctl system start -p docker

</div></div>
</pre>
<p>Meshery server supports customizing authentication flow callback URL, which can be configured in the following way</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>
<p><code>mesheryctl</code> uses your current Kubernetes context, your KUBECONFIG environment variable (<code>~/.kube/config</code> by default). Confirm if this Kubernetes cluster you want Meshery to interact with by running the following command: <code>kubectl config get-contexts</code>.</p>
<p>If there are multiple contexts in your kubeconfig file, specify the one you want to use with the <code>use-context</code> subcommand: <code>kubectl config use-context &lt;context-to-use&gt;</code>.</p>
<h3 id="upgrade-mesheryctl-using-brew">
	Upgrade <code>mesheryctl</code> using Brew
</h3>
<p>To upgrade <code>mesheryctl</code>, execute the following command.</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew upgrade mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<details>
<summary>
Example output of a successful upgrade.
</summary>
<pre><code>
➜  ~ brew upgrade mesheryctl
==> Upgrading 1 outdated package:
meshery/tap/mesheryctl 0.3.2 -> 0.3.4
==> Upgrading meshery/tap/mesheryctl
==> Downloading https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/download/v0.3.4/mesheryctl_0.3.4_Darwin_x86_64.zip
==> Downloading from https://github-production-release-asset-2e65be.s3.amazonaws.com/157554479/17522b00-2af0-11ea-8aef-cbfe8
######################################################################## 100.0%
🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/mesheryctl/0.3.4: 5 files, 10.2MB, built in 4 seconds
Removing: /usr/local/Cellar/mesheryctl/0.3.2... (5 files, 10.2MB)
Removing: /Users/lee/Library/Caches/Homebrew/mesheryctl--0.3.2.zip... (3.9MB)
==> Checking for dependents of upgraded formulae...

</code></pre>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<h1 id="overview">
	Overview
</h1>
<p>To set up and run Meshery on Linux or macOS, you will need to install <code>mesheryctl</code>. <code>mesheryctl</code> is the command-line interface (CLI) for Meshery. It is used to install, manage, and operate one or more Meshery deployments. <code>mesheryctl</code> can be installed via <code>bash</code>, is also available <a href="https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/latest">directly</a>, or through <a href="/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/brew/">Homebrew</a> or <a href="/v0.9/installation/windows/scoop/">Scoop</a>.</p>
<h1 id="brew">
	Brew
</h1>
<h3 id="prerequisites">
	Prerequisites
</h3>
<p>You need to have <code>Brew</code> installed on your <strong>Linux</strong> or <strong>macOS</strong> system to perform these actions.</p>
<h3 id="install-mesheryctl-using-brew">
	Install <code>mesheryctl</code> using Brew
</h3>
<p>To install <code>mesheryctl</code> using homebrew, execute the following commands.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew install mesheryctl
 </div></div>
</pre>
<p>You&rsquo;re ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>
<p>If you are running Meshery on Docker, execute the following command.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ mesheryctl system start -p docker

</div></div>
</pre>
<p>Meshery server supports customizing authentication flow callback URL, which can be configured in the following way</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
<div class="clipboardjs">
 $ MESHERY_SERVER_CALLBACK_URL=https://custom-host mesheryctl system start

</div></div>
</pre>
<p><code>mesheryctl</code> uses your current Kubernetes context, your KUBECONFIG environment variable (<code>~/.kube/config</code> by default). Confirm if this Kubernetes cluster you want Meshery to interact with by running the following command: <code>kubectl config get-contexts</code>.</p>
<p>If there are multiple contexts in your kubeconfig file, specify the one you want to use with the <code>use-context</code> subcommand: <code>kubectl config use-context &lt;context-to-use&gt;</code>.</p>
<h3 id="upgrade-mesheryctl-using-brew">
	Upgrade <code>mesheryctl</code> using Brew
</h3>
<p>To upgrade <code>mesheryctl</code>, execute the following command.</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
 $ brew upgrade mesheryctl
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<details>
<summary>
Example output of a successful upgrade.
</summary>
<pre><code>
➜  ~ brew upgrade mesheryctl
==> Upgrading 1 outdated package:
meshery/tap/mesheryctl 0.3.2 -> 0.3.4
==> Upgrading meshery/tap/mesheryctl
==> Downloading https://github.com/meshery/meshery/releases/download/v0.3.4/mesheryctl_0.3.4_Darwin_x86_64.zip
==> Downloading from https://github-production-release-asset-2e65be.s3.amazonaws.com/157554479/17522b00-2af0-11ea-8aef-cbfe8
######################################################################## 100.0%
🍺  /usr/local/Cellar/mesheryctl/0.3.4: 5 files, 10.2MB, built in 4 seconds
Removing: /usr/local/Cellar/mesheryctl/0.3.2... (5 files, 10.2MB)
Removing: /Users/lee/Library/Caches/Homebrew/mesheryctl--0.3.2.zip... (3.9MB)
==> Checking for dependents of upgraded formulae...
==> No dependents found!
</code></pre>
<br />
</details>
<h1 id="bash">
	Bash
</h1>
<p>To install or upgrade <code>mesheryctl</code> using <code>bash</code>, execute anyone of the following commands.</p>
<h4 id="option-1-only-install-mesheryctl-binary">
	Option 1: Only install <code>mesheryctl</code> binary
</h4>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | DEPLOY_MESHERY=false bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
#### Option 2: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Docker
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=docker bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
#### Option 3: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Kubernetes
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
#### Option 4: Install `mesheryctl` binary and Meshery adapter(s)
<p>Install <code>mesheryctl</code> binary and include one or more <a href="/v0.9/concepts/architecture/adapters/">adapters</a> to be deployed</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre">
 <div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">
  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | ADAPTERS=consul PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -
 </div></div>
 </pre>
<br />
<br />
### Start Meshery
You are ready to deploy Meshery `mesheryctl`. To do so, execute the following command.
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start</div></div>
 </pre>
<p>If you are running Meshery on Docker, execute the following command.</p>
 <pre class="codeblock-pre"><div class="codeblock">
 <div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl system start -p docker</div></div>
 </pre>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" standalone="yes"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
  <channel>
    <title>Install Meshery CLI on Linux or macOS on Documentation</title>
    <link>/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/</link>
    <description>Recent content in Install Meshery CLI on Linux or macOS on Documentation</description>
    <generator>Hugo</generator>
    <language>en</language>
    <atom:link href="/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/index.xml" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml" />
    <item>
      <title>Bash</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/bash/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/bash/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1 id=&#34;install-meshery-cli-with-bash&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install Meshery CLI with Bash&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;To install or upgrade &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; using &lt;code&gt;bash&lt;/code&gt;, execute anyone of the following commands.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h4 id=&#34;option-1-only-install-mesheryctl-binary&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Option 1: Only install &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; binary&#xA;&lt;/h4&gt;&#xA; &lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;&#xA;  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | DEPLOY_MESHERY=false bash -&#xA; &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA; &lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&lt;br /&gt;&#xA;&lt;br /&gt;&#xA;#### Option 2: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Docker&#xA; &lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;&#xA;  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=docker bash -&#xA; &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA; &lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&lt;br /&gt;&#xA;&lt;br /&gt;&#xA;#### Option 3: Install `mesheryctl` binary and deploy Meshery on Kubernetes&#xA; &lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;&#xA;  $ curl -L https://meshery.io/install | PLATFORM=kubernetes bash -&#xA; &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA; &lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&lt;br /&gt;&#xA;&lt;br /&gt;&#xA;#### Option 4: Install `mesheryctl` binary and Meshery adapter(s)&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Install &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; binary and include one or more &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/architecture/adapters/&#34;&gt;adapters&lt;/a&gt; to be deployed&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Brew</title>
      <link>/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/brew/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/installation/linux-mac/brew/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h1 id=&#34;install-meshery-cli-with-homebrew&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install Meshery CLI with Homebrew&#xA;&lt;/h1&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;prerequisites&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Prerequisites&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;You need to have &lt;code&gt;Brew&lt;/code&gt; installed on your &lt;strong&gt;Linux&lt;/strong&gt; or &lt;strong&gt;macOS&lt;/strong&gt; system to perform these actions.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;install-mesheryctl-using-brew&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Install &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; using Brew&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;To install &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl&lt;/code&gt; using homebrew, execute the following commands.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA; &lt;div class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;&#xA; $ brew install mesheryctl&#xA; &lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;You&amp;rsquo;re ready to run Meshery. To do so, execute the following command.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;pre class=&#34;codeblock-pre&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;codeblock&#34;&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;clipboardjs&#34;&gt;&#xA; $ mesheryctl system start&#xA;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;/pre&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;If you are running Meshery on Docker, execute the following command.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>
